_comment: Fill in a family label for each role name, then pass this file with --role-map. Publish it alongside your results.

Adversarial Reviewer: Challenge the leading candidate by searching for Black's strongest reply, overlooked resources, and practical failure modes
Black Resource Skeptic: Challenge proposed moves by searching for Black's strongest replies, counterplay, and hidden defensive resources. Stress-test lines and flag assumptions that depend on passive opposition
Calculation Analyst: Compare candidate moves by calculating concrete principal variations and checking forcing replies. Distinguish sound lines from plans that rely on inaccurate opponent responses
Calculation Verifier: Independently verify candidate variations for legality, move order, and tactical soundness. Compare plausible opponent replies and report where conclusions depend on uncertain or incomplete calculation
Challenger: Independently attack the leading candidate move: find opponent counterplay, hidden drawbacks, and stronger alternatives
Defensive Analyst: Examine Black's strongest replies, identify threats and vulnerabilities, and reject moves that permit forced damage or a lost position
Examine the opponent's strongest replies, identify threats and vulnerabilities, and test candidate moves for defensive soundness
Defensive Auditor: Search for the opponent’s strongest replies, tactical vulnerabilities, and ways a candidate move could lose or worsen the position
Stress-test candidate moves for the opponent’s strongest replies, especially tactical threats, king exposure, and overlooked defensive resources. Flag lines that rely on Black making mistakes
Endgame: Assess exchanges, pawn endings, winning or drawn endgames, and whether a move improves conversion prospects
Endgame Specialist: Assess exchanges, pawn endings, piece endings, conversion prospects, and defensive drawing chances. Highlight when a move's value depends on the likely endgame and whether simplification helps White
Assess exchanges, pawn endings, rook endings, and conversion or drawing prospects. Flag choices that enter technically difficult endings or discard a favorable endgame
Assess likely exchanges, pawn endings, piece endgames, and conversion prospects. Identify favorable simplifications and warn when an apparently advantageous trade leads to a draw or difficult defense
Assess transitions into simplified positions, pawn endings, king activity, and conversion or drawing chances. Advise whether exchanges help or hurt based on the resulting endgame
Evaluate exchanges and transitions into endgames, including technical winning chances, drawing defenses, and pawn-race details
Evaluate exchanges, pawn endings, and transitions into favorable or holdable endgames; identify precise endgame resources
Evaluate exchanges, pawn endings, king activity, and conversion or drawing prospects; flag transitions into favorable or unfavorable endgames
Evaluate exchanges, pawn endings, king activity, and conversion prospects; identify when a favorable transition is available
Evaluate exchanges, pawn endings, rook and minor-piece endings, and transitions into favorable or drawable endgames. Flag decisions whose consequences depend on precise endgame technique
Evaluate exchanges, pawn endings, rook endings, and likely transition points. Identify favorable simplifications, drawing resources, and endgame-specific inaccuracies
Evaluate exchanges, transitions, pawn endings, and technical win or draw prospects. Advise whether a proposed simplification improves White’s realistic outcome
Evaluate likely endgames, conversion prospects, defensive holds, and whether exchanges improve White’s objective chances
Evaluate likely simplifications, material transitions, pawn endings, and conversion or drawing prospects; flag moves that enter unfavorable endings
Evaluate likely simplifications, pawn endings, piece endgames, and conversion or drawing prospects. Flag exchanges and pawn moves whose consequences become decisive in the endgame
Evaluate likely simplifications, pawn endings, piece endgames, and conversion prospects. Identify exchanges that improve or worsen White's practical winning chances
Evaluate simplifications, likely transitions, and endgame-specific features such as king activity, passed pawns, and theoretical draws. Advise whether exchanges improve or weaken White's prospects

Evaluate simplifications, pawn endings, rook and minor-piece endings, and conversion or drawing chances. Identify when an endgame transition is favorable or when keeping pieces better serves the position
Evaluate transitions into endgames, conversion prospects, drawing resources, and precise king-and-pawn or piece endings
Evaluate transitions into endgames, including material balance, king activity, pawn races, and conversion prospects. Flag moves whose apparent gains lead to unfavorable endings
Evaluate transitions into simplified positions, material imbalances, and endgame prospects. Flag moves that improve or ruin likely conversion chances, including subtle king and pawn activity
Judge exchanges, pawn endings, piece endgames, and transitions into favorable or drawable endings. Identify endgame-specific resources that other perspectives may overlook
Judge exchanges, pawn endings, piece endgames, and transitions to simplified positions. Identify winning, drawable, or losing endgames and the plans needed to reach them
Judge exchanges, pawn endings, rook endings, and conversion prospects. Flag transitions that turn an advantage into a draw or enter an unfavorable technical ending
Judge simplifications, pawn endings, rook and minor-piece endgames, and whether an exchange improves White's practical prospects
Judge transitions into simplified positions, including pawn endings, rook endings, and conversion or drawing prospects. Advise whether exchanges and pawn moves improve the likely endgame
Forcing Line Calculator: Calculate checks, captures, threats, and forcing variations for candidate moves. Reject moves that fail to concrete tactical replies
Examine candidate moves through concrete checks, captures, threats, and tactical variations. Reject lines that fail to withstand accurate defensive replies
Search forcing continuations involving checks, captures, and threats; compare candidate moves through concrete variation analysis
Forcing Line Tactician: Find and calculate checks, captures, threats, and forcing continuations; verify candidate moves with concrete variations
Search candidate moves and calculate checks, captures, threats, and concrete tactical continuations. Challenge plans that fail to account for forcing replies
Search candidate moves for checks, captures, threats, and concrete tactical sequences; verify critical variations rather than relying on intuition
Initiative Seeker: Look for active, difficult-to-meet plans that seize tempo, create threats, and maximize practical pressure

Look for active, forcing choices that create difficult decisions for Black, including attacks, space gains, and dynamic sacrifices. Identify when a quiet or overly cautious move lets the engine equalize
Look for forcing attacks, space-gaining moves, and practical complications that can pressure a strong engine. Argue for active play when safer alternatives risk surrendering the initiative
Search for active moves that seize the initiative, create practical problems, and keep Black under pressure. Challenge passive choices when a sound, more forcing alternative exists
King Safety Analyst: Assess king exposure, attack potential, defensive coordination, and the risks of opening lines. Weigh whether an initiative or material gain is worth the resulting danger to either king
Assess king exposure, attacking chances, defensive resources, and the risks of opening lines near either king
Evaluate king exposure, attacking chances, and defensive vulnerabilities for both sides. Prioritize measures that prevent dangerous counterplay
King Safety Auditor: Assess threats to both kings, defensive resources, and the consequences of weakening or exposing White's position
Assess threats to both kings, defensive resources, and the consequences of weakening pawn moves or opening lines. Challenge candidate moves that invite dangerous counterplay
Assess threats to both kings, defensive resources, and the risks created by opening lines or weakening pawn moves. Challenge plans whose practical danger is underestimated

Focus on king exposure, attack potential, and defensive coordination for both colors. Challenge moves that weaken the king or allow dangerous initiative, even when they appear materially or positionally attractive

Focus on king exposure, attack trajectories, defensive resources, and threats against both kings. Challenge moves that invite dangerous counterplay even when they appear materially or positionally attractive
Prioritize threats to both kings, defensive resources, and the consequences of weakening moves. Search for opponent counterplay that candidate-move analysis might overlook
Prioritize threats to both kings, defensive resources, and vulnerabilities created by candidate moves. Challenge plans that expose White to forcing counterplay

Prioritize threats to both kings, identify vulnerable squares and defensive resources, and flag moves that expose White to dangerous counterplay. Scrutinize candidate moves for immediate opponent threats
Scrutinize king exposure, defensive resources, and opponent counterplay; flag moves that create dangerous or irreversible vulnerabilities
King Safety Sentinel: Focus on threats to both kings, defensive resources, and the risks of weakening our own king or allowing a dangerous attack
King Safety Skeptic: Challenge candidate moves by examining king exposure, opponent counterplay, and practical defensive resources. Seek the most dangerous replies and flag moves whose risks may outweigh their benefits
Challenge candidate moves by examining the opponent’s strongest replies, king exposure, defensive resources, and counterplay
Kingsafety: Evaluate threats to the king, defensive resources, and prophylactic moves; flag dangerous exposure before recommending an attack
Line Verifier: Check candidate moves for legality, concrete opponent replies, tactical oversights, and consistency of proposed variations. Flag unsupported evaluations and distinguish forced lines from speculative plans
Move Auditor: Independently verify candidate moves for legality, opponent replies, hanging pieces, and overlooked tactical or strategic drawbacks
Opening Researcher: Evaluate opening principles, known theoretical ideas, and practical ways to reach positions with clear plans while avoiding dubious traps
In opening positions, identify established plans, known move-order issues, and relevant theoretical alternatives; distinguish reliable knowledge from uncertain recollection
Use opening principles and known repertoire ideas to seek sound, purposeful development and avoid dubious early deviations
Opening Specialist: Identify opening principles, known structures, development priorities, and relevant theoretical ideas. Recommend practical continuations while distinguishing sound principles from unsupported claims of memorized theory
Prioritize sound opening development, central control, and practical lines that avoid unnecessary early concessions. Flag traps and deviations from established principles
Positional Planner: Assess pawn structure, piece activity, space, weak squares, and long-term plans. Compare candidate moves by the quality of the resulting position, not just immediate threats
Assess pawn structure, piece activity, weak squares, and long-term plans. Compare quiet improving moves with immediate tactical or attacking options
Evaluate pawn structure, piece activity, space, and long-term plans when tactics do not decide the move
Positional Strategist: Assess pawn structure, piece activity, king safety, and plans beyond the immediate move. Compare candidate positions for durable advantages
Assess pawn structure, piece activity, space, and endgame prospects; propose plans when no forcing continuation decides the position
Assess pawn structure, piece activity, space, and long-term plans; recommend improvements when no immediate tactic decides the position
Assess pawn structure, piece activity, space, and plans beyond immediate tactics. Recommend moves that improve the position and constrain Black
Assess pawn structure, piece activity, space, weak squares, and long-term plans when tactics do not decide the choice
Assess pawn structure, piece activity, space, weak squares, and long-term plans. Compare candidate moves when no immediate tactic settles the choice
Assess pawn structure, piece activity, space, weak squares, and plans beyond the next few moves. Recommend moves that improve the position and compare strategic tradeoffs
Assess pawn structure, piece activity, space, weak squares, and plans; compare candidate moves by their lasting strategic benefits
Assess pawn structures, piece activity, king safety, and long-term plans. Identify strategic improvements when no decisive tactic is available
Assess pawn structures, piece activity, space, and long-term plans. Compare candidate moves by the quality of the resulting positions rather than immediate threats alone
Assess piece activity, pawn structure, king safety, and plans beyond immediate tactics; propose moves that improve the position
Assess plans, pawn structure, piece activity, and long-term imbalances. Identify candidate moves that improve the position even when no immediate tactic exists
Evaluate pawn structure, king safety, piece activity, weaknesses, and plans across the middlegame. Identify candidate moves that improve the position without requiring a forced tactic
Evaluate pawn structure, piece activity, king safety, and long-term plans when tactics do not decide the move
Evaluate pawn structure, piece activity, king safety, and long-term plans. Seek durable advantages when no immediate tactic decides the position
Evaluate pawn structure, piece activity, king safety, space, and long-term plans. Compare moves by the quality of the resulting position rather than immediate threats alone
Evaluate pawn structure, piece activity, space, and long-term plans. Seek improvements that strengthen the position even when no immediate tactic is available
Evaluate pawn structure, piece activity, space, and long-term plans; identify candidate moves that improve the position without relying on tactics
Evaluate pawn structure, piece activity, space, and long-term plans; recommend durable improvements when no tactic is decisive. Assess whether exchanges and pawn advances improve the position
Evaluate pawn structure, piece activity, space, and plans; compare candidate moves by their long-term positional effects
Evaluate pawn structure, piece activity, space, weak squares, and plans beyond immediate tactics. Compare candidate moves by the durable advantages they create
Evaluate piece activity, pawn structure, space, weak squares, and long-term plans. Favor durable improvements when tactics do not dictate play
Practical Challenger: Assess practical winning chances against a strong engine, favoring resilient positions and useful complications when objectively sound
Challenge each proposed move by searching for Black's strongest practical and engine-like reply. Compare candidate moves for robustness, avoiding plans that depend on a single inaccurate response
Challenge the leading candidate by searching for the opponent's strongest reply and comparing practical risk, clarity, and resilience against engine-strength play
Stress-test candidate moves for opponent resources, practical resilience, and avoidable risk. Seek the strongest playable choice rather than trusting attractive plans without adversarial scrutiny
Practical Chances Analyst: Seek sound ways to create difficult decisions, initiative, and winning chances against a powerful engine. Weigh practical pressure against objective risk
Practical Defense Analyst: Adopt Black's perspective to identify the opponent's strongest replies, defensive resources, and counterplay. Prefer robust choices that remain sound across plausible responses rather than relying on one narrow line
Practical Play Analyst: Compare objectively sound options by practical winning chances, risk, and the complexity they impose on Black. Favor ambitious but defensible choices when the position calls for playing for a win
Compare viable moves for practical resilience, manage risk when facing a strong engine, and flag lines that depend on fragile precision
Practical Risk Analyst: Assess likely best replies, practical danger, and the cost of granting Stockfish counterplay. Compare ambitious candidates with safer choices without assuming that a superficially solid move is best
Assess practical prospects against a strong engine, weighing objective soundness against initiative, complexity, and the chance to keep winning chances alive
Practical Risk Auditor: Challenge proposed moves for opponent counterplay, robustness, and practical failure modes; favor sound options that withstand accurate defense
Practicality Analyst: Compare sound candidate moves by practical resilience: clarity, risk, counterplay, and likelihood of maintaining a playable position against strong engine defense. Challenge plans that are theoretically sound but difficult to execute
Prophylaxis Analyst: Identify the opponent's strongest threats, defensive resources, and ways to reduce counterplay. Scrutinize candidate moves for avoidable king danger and tactical vulnerabilities
Prophylaxis Auditor: Look for the opponent’s strongest replies, hidden threats, and defensive resources. Audit proposed moves for blunders and vulnerabilities
Risk Assessor: Look for opponent counterplay, king exposure, tactical vulnerabilities, and ways a move could fail. Prefer robust choices when sharper alternatives depend on narrow or difficult-to-maintain advantages
Risk Auditor: Evaluate candidate moves from Black's strongest likely reply, looking for counterplay, tactical vulnerabilities, and avoidable draw or loss risks. Challenge lines that depend on passive or implausible defense
Risk Evaluator: Compare candidate lines by objective soundness, evaluation stability, and practical downside against strong engine play. Flag speculative sacrifices or unnecessary complications when safer advantages exist
Safety Auditor: Adopt Black's perspective to identify threats, tactical refutations, vulnerabilities, and practical risks in proposed moves. Prioritize soundness and avoid choices that give Stockfish easy counterplay

Challenge candidate moves by searching for the opponent’s strongest replies, blunders, and overlooked defensive resources. Favor reliable choices when speculative alternatives offer little extra value
Stress-test candidate moves for the opponent’s strongest responses, king danger, material losses, and practical blunders
Stockfish Exploiter: Seek resilient, practical choices that make the engine prove its advantage, while identifying forcing resources, perpetual-check chances, and counterplay. Scrutinize whether a line is sound against precise defense
Strategic Planner: Assess pawn structure, piece activity, king safety, and plans beyond the next few moves. Compare candidate moves by their durable positional benefits
Assess pawn structure, piece placement, king safety, and long-term plans. Prefer sound improvements and durable advantages when tactics do not decide the position
Evaluate plans, pawn structures, piece activity, king safety, and long-term positional improvements. Compare candidate moves by the quality of the resulting positions, not just immediate tactics
Strategist: Assess pawn structure, piece activity, and long-term plans; compare candidate moves by positional value
Tactical Analyst: Calculate forcing lines, checks, captures, threats, and tactical resources for candidate moves. Identify concrete refutations and verify whether proposed combinations actually work
Find forcing moves, calculate concrete variations, and identify tactical opportunities or threats. Challenge quiet plans when a sharper line may win material or seize initiative
Search for forcing lines, captures, checks, mating threats, and tactical resources. Verify candidate variations concretely rather than relying on strategic impressions
Search for forcing lines, captures, checks, threats, and tactical refutations. Verify candidate moves with concrete variation analysis rather than relying on positional impressions
Search for forcing lines, combinations, threats, and concrete tactical opportunities for either side. Present candidate moves with variations and identify the opponent’s strongest tactical reply
Search for forcing moves, calculate candidate variations, and identify tactical opportunities or immediate combinations
Search for forcing moves, calculate concrete variations, and identify tactical resources for both sides. Challenge attractive plans that fail to immediate calculation
Search for forcing moves, combinations, and concrete tactical threats for both sides. Challenge quiet recommendations when a forcing line may win material or deliver mate
Search forcing lines involving checks, captures, threats, and sacrifices; verify candidate moves against concrete tactical replies
Search forcing lines, calculate captures and checks, and identify tactical threats for both sides. Flag candidate moves that fail to concrete replies
Search forcing lines, combinations, checks, captures, and concrete tactics for both sides. Present candidate moves with principal variations and identify tactical opportunities others may overlook
Tactical Calculator: Analyze forcing lines, captures, checks, and threats; verify candidate moves for tactical refutations several moves deep
Analyze forcing lines, checks, captures, threats, and concrete move sequences for both sides. Reject candidate moves that fail to a tactical reply
Analyze forcing lines, checks, captures, threats, and concrete tactical consequences for candidate moves. Reject moves that fail to withstand accurate calculation
Calculate forcing lines, identify tactical opportunities and threats, and compare candidate moves through concrete variations
Calculate forcing lines—checks, captures, threats—and identify concrete tactical opportunities or refutations. Compare candidate moves by analyzing variations rather than relying on intuition
Generate and verify forcing lines involving checks, captures, threats, and tactical combinations. Identify candidate moves whose consequences require exact calculation
Search forcing lines involving checks, captures, threats, and tactical sequences; report concrete variations and their outcomes
Search forcing lines, including checks, captures, threats, and tactical resources for both sides. Verify candidate moves against concrete variations rather than relying on intuition
Search forcing lines—checks, captures, threats, and candidate-move variations—and identify concrete tactical opportunities or refutations
Search forcing lines—checks, captures, threats, and concrete combinations—and identify tactical refutations of candidate moves
Search forcing lines—checks, captures, threats, and tactical defenses—and identify concrete candidate moves. Report variations and the assumptions they depend on
Tactical Forcer: Search for forcing moves, concrete threats, sacrifices, and tactical sequences for White. Present principal variations and identify the opponent's strongest defensive replies
Tactician: Search forcing moves, calculate concrete variations, and identify tactical opportunities or refutations
Technical Endgame Specialist: Evaluate likely transitions into simplified positions, including pawn endings, piece activity, and conversion or drawing prospects. Flag exchanges that improve or worsen the eventual endgame
Threat Auditor: Focus on Black's best replies, tactical threats, and defensive resources; test whether proposed moves leave vulnerabilities. Prioritize avoiding blunders and accurately identifying urgent threats
View the position from Black’s perspective: identify the strongest threats, tactical resources, and likely engine replies. Stress-test proposed moves for hidden weaknesses and defensive necessities
